source_text: XI. Ὁ δὲ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Θηρία ἔχω, τούτοις σε παραβαλῶ, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσῃς. Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Κάλει· ἀμετάθετος γὰρ ἡμῖν ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν κρειττόνων ἐπὶ τὰ χείρω μετάνοια· καλὸν δὲ μετατίθεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν χαλεπῶν ἐπὶ τὰ δίκαια. Ὁ δὲ πάλιν πρὸς αὐτόν· Πυρί σε ποιῶ δαπανηθῆναι, εἰ τῶν θηρίων καταφρονεῖς, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσῃς. Ὁ δὲ Πολύκαρπος εἶπεν· Πῦρ ἀπειλεῖς τὸ πρὸς ὥραν καιόμενον καὶ μετ᾽ ὀλίγον σβεννύμενον· ἀγνοεῖς γὰρ τὸ τῆς μελλούσης κρίσεως καὶ αἰωνίου κολάσεως τοῖς ἀσεβέσι τηρούμενον πῦρ. Ἀλλὰ τί βραδύνεις; Φέρε ὃ βούλει.
pass_a_gloss: And the proconsul said: I have beasts, to these I will throw you, unless you repent. And he said: Call them; for unchangeable for us is the repentance from the better things to the worse; but it is good to change from the hard things to the just things. And he again to him: I will cause you to be consumed by fire, if you despise the beasts, unless you repent. And Polycarp said: You threaten fire that burns for an hour and after a little is quenched; for you do not know the fire of the coming judgment and of eternal punishment kept for the ungodly. But why do you delay? Bring what you wish.
pass_b_english: The proconsul said, I have wild beasts, and to them I will throw you, unless you recant. He answered, Call them, for the turning from the better to the worse is a turning we cannot change, yet it is good to turn from what is harsh to what is righteous.

He said to him again, I will have you consumed by fire, if you despise the beasts, unless you recant. And Polycarp said, You threaten fire that burns for an hour and after a little while is quenched, for you do not know the fire of the coming judgment and of the eternal punishment kept for the ungodly. But why do you delay? Bring whatever you wish.

choices.reason: summon the beasts, not send for them
